[b]Disclaimer: my "non-recommendation" is independent of the use of generative AI. You know what you signed up for when you read the store page.[/b] I am thankful for this being a free game, as there is very little to do in this game. This is a good proof of concept for a larger game, but I don't feel confident recommending it until there is a real game that does the obvious continuation of what we see in here. As others have pointed out, the entire campaign lasts 30 minutes, give or take. There are not many options for spells and the rooms are the same, in the same order, so there is not much room for variety. Maybe the enemie spawning positions are randomised, but I didn't even notice - because this game can be beaten without breaking a sweat if you know what spells you need. This is why I ultimately cannot recommend the game in its current form. The only dungeon is good as a tutorial dungeon since you can pretty much beat it hitless once you know what spells to use, but it really needs to expand in multiple directions. In fact, the ending of the game serves you a way in which the game could continue on a silver platter: [spoiler]now that the magician can actually use mana, she could have a tiny mana bar alongside the dice rolls, and have a goal of gathering enough money to actually pay off her debt. In fact, why stop there? Let us just see how she meets with the other magicians, see how she makes friends who collaborate with her, maybe even forming a whole team to raid larger dungeons. Her gimmick is using dice to bypass her initial low pool of mana; other people can have other classes or different magic niches.[/spoiler] And with that out of the way, I will say what the anti-AI crowd is thinking: if (hopefully when) you make the sequel, please, actually hire a team of people to make the assets instead.
